s1.syndrome_frame: Facial swelling and calcified mass with a chronic time course
key_facts: 1-week history of right facial swelling and cellulitis
mass in right maxillary molar area noticed 6 months earlier
extensive, well-demarcated, dense amorphous irregular calcified lesion in right maxilla

mass in right maxillary molar area noticed 6 months earlier
extensive, well-demarcated, dense amorphous irregular calcified lesion in right maxilla

shortlist.label: Complex odontoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of a calcified mass in the jaw with a chronic time course

shortlist.label: Calcifying epithelial odontogenic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the radiographic findings of a well-demarcated, dense amorphous irregular calcified lesion

shortlist.label: Adenomatoid odontogenic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Compatible with the intraoral calcified mass and missing teeth, with a possible chronic time course

shortlist.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Fits the description of a hard swelling over the right maxilla with an associated intraoral calcified mass

shortlist.label: Fibro-osseous lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain the extensive, well-demarcated, dense amorphous irregular calcified lesion in the right maxilla

raw.rationale: The presence of a calcified mass and missing teeth, along with the radiographic appearance of a well-demarcated, dense amorphous irregular calcified lesion, is consistent with a complex odontoma.

rejected.label: Calcifying epithelial odontogenic tumor
rejected.why: Less likely due to the absence of characteristic radiolucent or mixed radiolucent and radiopaque appearance

rejected.label: Adenomatoid odontogenic tumor
rejected.why: Typically associated with an unerupted tooth, which is not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
rejected.why: Usually presents as a well-defined radiolucent lesion with variable amounts of internal calcification, not matching the described dense calcified lesion

rejected.label: Fibro-osseous lesion
rejected.why: A broader category that includes various lesions, but the specific findings point more directly to a complex odontoma
